definitions.explanation: A gift given by the hosts to guests at a wedding reception or other formal celebration as a token of thanks for attending.

examples.japanese: {引|ひ}き{出物|でもの}を{選|えら}ぶ。
{結婚式|けっこんしき}の{引|ひ}き{出物|でもの}にカタログギフトが{人気|にんき}だ。
examples.english: Catalog gifts are popular as wedding favors.

examples.japanese: {披露宴|ひろうえん}の{帰|かえ}りに{引|ひ}き{出物|でもの}の{入|はい}った{紙袋|かみぶくろ}を{受|う}け{取|と}った。
examples.english: On the way home from the reception, I received a paper bag containing the wedding favor.

notes:
CULTURAL CONTEXT:
At Japanese weddings, guests typically give {御祝儀|ごしゅうぎ} (monetary gifts) to the couple. In return, the couple provides {引|ひ}き{出物|でもの} to each guest. Common {引|ひ}き{出物|でもの} include tableware, catalog gifts, sweets ({引|ひ}き{菓子|がし}), and specialty food items.

ETYMOLOGY:
Originally referred to horses or other valuable items "pulled out" ({引|ひ}き{出|だ}す) and presented to guests at banquets in the Heian period.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{引|ひ}き{出物|でもの}を{選|えら}ぶ (to choose wedding favors)
・{引|ひ}き{出物|でもの}を{贈|おく}る (to give wedding favors)
・カタログ{式|しき}の{引|ひ}き{出物|でもの} (catalog-style wedding favors)
